1: Chapter 1: A Guest on a Rainy Night
The rain in Qingshi had been falling for three full days. Lin Xiaoyu's older sister had gone to the capital in spring, and since then this small pharmacy in town had been left to her alone.
After dark, she closed the doors and windows, counted the day's earnings, blew out the oil lamp, and went upstairs.
She had just lain down when urgent knocking came from downstairs, followed by a man's voice: "Is anyone there?"
Outside the door stood a young man soaked to the skin, his left arm wrapped in blood-soaked bandages. He said his name was Bai Yun and that he was a member of the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need my wound bandaged," Bai Yun said quietly. "Is three thousand five hundred wen enough?"
He took from his chest a letter wrapped in oiled paper: "This letter must be delivered to Qingfeng before May 18."
While she bandaged him, he said with a bitter smile, "If my fiancée knew I was knocking on a young woman's door in the middle of the night, she would definitely be jealous."
Lin Xiaoyu did not take his money; she only said, "I'll take you up the mountain first thing tomorrow morning."
2: At daybreak, the two set off. Lin Xiaoyu carried a bamboo basket on her back, containing dried food, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain, they met an old woodcutter, Zhou Dashan. The old man set down his axe and lowered his voice: yesterday evening, three outsiders had been asking around at the town gate about an injured young man.
"Xiaoyu, take the small path," Zhou Dashan said. "The main road isn't safe." Lin Xiaoyu thanked him.
The small path was narrow and slippery. Lin Xiaoyu walked ahead, each step sure and steady. Bai Yun followed behind, not saying a word.

By noon the rain had stopped, and the mountain mist slowly dispersed, revealing the roof of Qingfeng Temple in the distance. At the temple gate stood a nun named Zhao Qiuyue, the nun in charge of receiving guests.
Zhao Qiuyue took the letter, looked at the red seal on the envelope, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting for this letter for 2 years."
Bai Yun said to Lin Xiaoyu, "I owe you my life." Lin Xiaoyu smiled. "Then next time you come, help me fix the roof of my medicine shop." Bai Yun stayed at the temple.
In the evening, Lin Xiaoyu descended the mountain alone. By the time she got home, it was already dark; she lit a lamp and sat behind the counter for a long time.
